title: 11 types of fracture
question: 11 types of fracture. Which one have you had?
hook: Not every broken bone breaks the *same* way.
intro: Here are 11 types of fracture you should know.

types.name: transverse
types.label: TRANSVERSE
lines: [Transverse](tɹænzvˈɜːɹs). A straight break, right across the bone.

types.name: oblique
types.label: OBLIQUE
lines: Oblique. The break runs at an *angle* across the bone.

types.name: spiral
types.label: SPIRAL
lines: Spiral. A *twisting* force makes the break [wind](wˈaɪnd) around the bone.

types.name: greenstick
types.label: GREENSTICK
lines: Greenstick. The bone cracks on one side and *bends* on the other.
It's common in kids, because their bones are more flexible.

types.name: displaced
types.label: DISPLACED
lines: Displaced. The broken ends shift [out of](ˈaʊt ʌv) line.
They often have to be set back in place.

types.name: comminuted
types.label: COMMINUTED
lines: [Comminuted](kˈɑːmᵻnuːɾᵻd). The bone *shatters* into three or more pieces.

types.name: segmental
types.label: SEGMENTAL
lines: Segmental. *Two* breaks leave a floating piece in the middle.

types.name: avulsion
types.label: AVULSION
lines: [Avulsion](əvˈʌlʃən). A tendon or ligament pulls off a chip of bone.

types.name: impacted
types.label: IMPACTED
lines: [Impacted](ɪmpˈæktᵻd). The broken ends are *jammed* into each other.

types.name: buckle
types.label: BUCKLE
lines: Buckle, or torus. The bone bulges instead of breaking through.
You often see it in kids' wrists.

types.name: stress
types.label: STRESS
lines: Stress fracture. A *tiny* crack from repeated force.

outro: Send this to the friend who's always breaking something.
why: Transverse: straight across. Oblique: at an angle. Spiral: twisted around the bone. Greenstick: cracked on one side, bent on the other (kids). Displaced: ends out of line. Comminuted: 3+ pieces. Segmental: two breaks, a floating piece. Avulsion: a tendon or ligament pulls off a chip. Impacted: ends jammed together. Buckle (torus): the bone bulges (kids' wrists). Stress: a tiny crack from repeated force.
